Shared fakes for the S06b run-buffer tests (not collected: no test_ prefix).

  Clock          a controllable clock; the buffer's `_now` and the fake Redis's TTLs
                 both read it, so an idle expiry, a hard cap and a refresh can be
                 crossed in a test without sleeping.
  FakeRunRedis   the thin interface codeagent.buffer talks to (`command(*args)` and
                 `atomic(commands)`, see buffer.RedisLike), backed by a small
                 interpreter for exactly the Redis commands the buffer uses:
                 HGET HMGET HSETNX HSET HINCRBY RPUSH RPUSHX LRANGE EXPIRE (with LT)
                 DEL EXISTS TTL. It behaves like Redis where it matters here:
                   - everything is stored as a string and returned as one (HINCRBY
                     and the list lengths are ints), a missing key reads as None / [];
                   - RPUSHX does nothing (returns 0) when the list does not exist;
                   - EXPIRE returns 1 / 0, and `EXPIRE ... LT` only ever shortens;
                   - TTLs run on the Clock; an expired key is gone for every command;
                   - `atomic` runs its commands under one lock, so nothing interleaves.
                 It also records every request (its commands and its size in bytes,
                 counted the way the REST body would be: the length of every
                 argument) so a test can assert that no single request, and no single
                 reply, comes near a reques

Shared helpers for the S04 device-socket tests (not collected: no test_ prefix).

Builds on S03's devices_testkit (Clock, FakeStore, SECRET, ...) rather than
re-implementing a device registry:

  WsFakeStore   devices_testkit.FakeStore plus the one store method S04 adds to
                eo.devices.PgStore (credential_is_revoked), call counters, and
                switches that make a store call fail. A subclass, not an edit of
                the shared kit, so this patch cannot conflict with another patch
                touching devices_testkit.py.
  Rig           one FastAPI app with the S04 router behind a TestClient, a fresh
                connection registry, a fresh handshake limiter on a fake clock,
                and injectable socket settings -- everything monkeypatched, so
                no state leaks between tests.
  FakeDevice    a device that knows how to speak the protocol to the Rig:
                connect, hello, send an envelope, read one.
  ScriptedHandler
                a stand-in for the run manager (S06): answers each client
                message with the server lines a golden transcript has next.

Nothing here imports jsonschema at module level: the server loads the protocol
validator lazily, and these helpers must stay importable where it is absent.

Shared fakes for the S03 device-pairing tests (not collected: no test_ prefix).

  Clock         a controllable clock, so expiry and lock-out windows can be
                crossed without sleeping.
  FakeStore     an in-memory eo.devices.PgStore with the same atomic
                semantics (single collection of a credential, revocation

                show a lock-out lifting.

  Harness       a FastAPI app with the devices router, a TestClient, and a
                switchable "signed-in user" standing in for require_auth.

files.module_doc:
Shared helpers for the S07 agent-loop tests (not collected: no test_ prefix).

  ScriptedAdapter   a ModelAdapter that plays a script: one entry per model call. An entry is a Reply (text, tool
                    calls, usage), a list of raw events (HANG waits for ever, so a test can cancel mid-stream), or
                    an exception to raise. It records every ModelRequest it was given and how many streams were
                    closed (a cancelled loop must close the provider stream).
  FakeBroker        the loop's side of S09's ToolBroker: propose() / cancel_all(). Each call is answered by a
                    behaviour (ok, error, denied, timeout, disconnected, hold until cancelled, approve-then-ok),
                    and the fake records the calls, how many were in flight at once and the run's state at the
                    moment of each call. It emits nothing: the real-broker tests use codeagent.broker itself.
  Rig               one run in the real S06 modules (runs, buffer, run_manager, run_guard) over the in-memory
                    twins of run_manager_testkit.World, plus a recording emitter and a fake device connection.
                    Only the model, the broker (mostly), tool_budget and the connection are fakes.

Fake secrets are built at run time (gitleaks flags literals shaped like keys); nothing here is one.

files.module_doc:
Shared fakes for the S06c run-manager tests (not collected: no test_ prefix).

The run manager glues three things that already have in-memory twins, so this file only
adds the missing pieces and ties them together:

  World             one object holding every stand-in, with ONE clock for all of them:
                      store     runs_testkit.FakeRunStore    (the `runs` table)
                      sweep     FakeSweepStore               (the cross-account read)
                      redis     buffer_testkit.FakeRunRedis  (the run buffer)
                      guard     FakeGuardRedis               (eo/run_guard's keys)
                    advance(seconds) moves all clocks together; `now` is the same
                    instant as a datetime.
  FakeGuardRedis    the few commands eo/run_guard uses (get/set/delete/incr/incrby/
                    expire), in memory, so a test can assert that nothing is left.
  FakeSweepStore    codeagent.run_manager.PgSweepStore over the FakeRunStore's rows:
                    open runs idle since before a cutoff, keyset-paged on (updated_at, id).
  start_payload()   a run.start payload that is valid against protocol/v1.

files.module_doc:
Shared fakes for the S06 run-manager tests (not collected: no test_ prefix).

  Clock          a controllable clock, so timestamps can be told apart without
                 sleeping.
  FakeRunStore   an in-memory codeagent.runs.PgRunStore with the same atomic
                 semantics: one lock makes every method atomic, like a single SQL
                 statement; `move` only succeeds if the row is still in the state
                 the caller read (the conditional UPDATE); the parallel-run cap is
                 counted inside the same critical section as the insert / resume
                 (the advisory lock). It also enforces the two things the
                 migration's trigger enforces, so a test that tries to cheat the
                 state machine through the store fails the way the database would:
                 a terminal row never changes state, and counters never decrease.
                 The SQL itself, the trigger and the policies are covered by
                 tests/integration/test_runs_pg.py.

                 Two hooks make races deterministic instead of lucky:
                   after_get(user_id, run_id, row)   called after every `get`, outside
                                                     the lock -- put a barrier here so
                                                     every racer has READ before any
                                                     of them WRITES;
                   before_move(call)                 called at
